mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average indicates an ongoing monetary easing cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 7.5% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 7.5% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline in the latest month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average, manufacturing sector weakness leads to reduced corporate capital expenditure and lower earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO is below its 6-month moving average, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS increases month-over-month, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with a rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates a policy response to inflation that typically leads to a temporary equity boost followed by a sell-off as inflation persists, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL rises in the latest month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL rises, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong consumer demand regime defined by housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both exceeding their 12-month moving averages, corporate revenue growth is robust, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS are both above their 12-month moving averages, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.
